author: Donnell Coley
title: ECU basketball: Pirates rout Roadrunners, end home losing skid - NewsBreak
text:
By Donnell Coley ,
9 hours ago
By the time Isaiah Mbeng hit his third 3-pointer Wednesday, East Carolina had already doubled up visiting UTSA.
The transfer guard would end with a career-high points total and ultimately help ECU ease to an 88-72 win inside Minges Coliseum.
Mbeng scored 18 off the strength of four triples. It marked an all-around effective outing to go with eight rebounds and a team-best six assists.
The performance also highlighted a balanced ECU (8-16, 3-8 American) effort that saw the conference's top scorer, Jordan Riley , only have to put in 19 points – four shy of his average.
"It's big, for sure. I know the work I put in, so it's good to finally see some of it show," Mbeng said. "But hopefully, it's just a spark going forward."
His spark helped free other teammates to score throughout the matchup against a lowly UTSA (4-20, 0-12) group that dropped its 17th straight.
A season-high five Pirates ended in double figures, including Demitri Gardner's 15 points. The midseason transfer earned the game's first double-digit lead when he converted a fastbreak layup to make it 24-13 midway through the opening half.
Mbeng's trey, with eight minutes to go, fell through and pushed the margin to 32-16. The Pirates maintained the huge advantage through the halftime horn as Gardner drained a corner 3 as time expired to put them up 46-31.
Pirates center Giovanni Emejuru dominated both ends, finishing with a 12-points 12-rebounds double-double and three blocks. Most of his damage came in the second period, when dropped 10 to help keep the Roadrunners from closing in.
Riley, meanwhile, failed to reach 30 points for the first time in nearly two weeks. He still scored 13 in the second half to help salt things.
UTSA had four players reach double figures, led by Brent Moss' 15.
ECU coach Mike Schwartz witnessed a collective effort, with his team leading for more than 35 minutes and the margin growing to as many as 22 points late.
"To be quite honest … it's extremely refreshing," said the fourth-year head man. "It's something we've kind of prided ourselves on in our first three seasons prior to this … and we haven't quite been able to hit that balance and versatility this season.
So to have a game like this in mid-February is exciting. I think it does so much for our ball club to see multiple guys step up."
The victory was also Schwartz's first at home since December. It followed five straight losses at Williams Arena.
ECU on Saturday tries to extend its road streak to three consecutive wins, playing Rice in Texas at 2 p.m.
Pirates WBB gets past USF
The women's basketball team Tuesday pulled away from Tulane on the road, 65-61.
ECU (18-8, 10-2 American) remains second in the conference, and earned its first win at Tulane in 11 years.
Transfer guard Kennedy Fauntleroy led three Pirates in double figures, netting a team-high 23 points.
Mecailin Marshall kept her squad in it, scoring a career-best 34 points and helping Tulane go up 33-32 at halftime.
Keanna Rembert, who had 12 points, grabbed an offensive rebound and tossed it in to beat the buzzer and give her Pirates a 48-46 lead entering the fourth.
The Pirates claimed a 9-0 run to open the final period, then held the Green Wave scoreless until the 5:22 mark to go up double digits. Their lead dipped to as low as four, but the visitors held off a final-minute Tulane rally.
Up next, ECU travels to American foe Temple Saturday for a 2 p.m. tip on ESPN+.
